title: Harness facts
description: The facts of one agent harness: the program and the nix package that hold it, how it reaches a model, the arguments of a launch, of an isolated launch, of the version probe and of a headless run, and the files and directories the harness reads. A tool ships these facts for every harness it supports, and a harnesses.d/<name>.json file overrides the ones it names.

path.description: A slash-separated path relative to the directory it belongs to.

facts.description: The members of the facts of a harness. A shipped facts file sets every required member; an override sets only the members it changes.

name.description: The agent type the facts describe. An override file is named <name>.json.

description.description: Why the facts are as they are, for a reader of the file.

binary.description: The program to start: a name on the path or an absolute path.

nixPackage.description: The nix package that provides the binary.

protocol.description: The model API wire protocol the harness speaks, absent when it chooses its own service or takes any provider.

access.description: How the harness obtains model access: from a provider route, or from the login of its own vendor.

providerEnv.description: True when the harness reads the provider environment.

providerArgs.description: True when the harness takes the provider arguments.

launchArgs.description: The arguments every launch passes first, such as a subcommand.

sandboxArgs.description: The arguments a launch inside an isolation adds, such as the one that turns off the command sandbox or the permission prompts of the harness.

versionArgs.description: The arguments that make the binary print its version.

userConfigPaths.description: The smallest set of paths below the home directory that the harness needs from the user, which an isolation binds.

configHome.description: The directory the harness keeps its configuration in, and the variable that moves it.

instructionFile.description: The project file the harness reads as its instructions.

skillsDir.description: The directory below a project or the home directory that the harness reads skills from.

plugin.description: Where a plugin of the harness keeps its parts, relative to the plugin or to the marketplace root.

headless.description: The arguments of a run that takes one prompt and exits.

args.description: The arguments that make the run non-interactive.

hermeticArgs.description: The arguments that keep the run from reading the configuration, sessions and servers of the machine.

output.description: The arguments of each output format, by format name.

options.description: Named options. Each is a list of arguments, and {value} in an argument stands for the value the run gives the option.

skillPrompt.description: The prompt that invokes a skill by name: {skill} stands for the skill and {prompt} for the request.
